rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is nonexistent, so the first experiment should establish a baseline. This tests a simple RNA-only model with singleprofile and PCA encoding to measure baseline validation accuracy, isolating the effect of RNA representation and profile setting. It clarifies whether RNA-only models can achieve reasonable performance, informing subsequent comparisons with multimodal approaches.

The existing evidence shows that config_001 (RNA-only, singleprofile, PCA) achieves 0.4849 validation accuracy. This experiment tests the impact of switching to multiprofile with avgpool aggregation, isolating the effect of profile setting and aggregation. It balances exploration by testing a key design choice (multiprofile) while keeping RNA encoder and fusion consistent, providing critical insight into whether multiprofile improves performance and which aggregation method (avgpool vs transformer) is more effective.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile (config_002) outperforms singleprofile (config_001) for RNA-only models. This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool (used in config_002) with transformer aggregation further improves performance in multiprofile RNA-only models. It isolates the effect of aggregation method, a critical design choice, while keeping RNA encoder and profile setting consistent. This clarifies whether more complex aggregation mechanisms provide incremental gains, balancing exploration of key components with exploitation of the promising multiprofile direction.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile with avgpool aggregation (config_002) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (a different representation) while keeping other settings identical isolates the impact of the RNA encoder choice. This addresses a key design decision with sparse evidence, balancing exploration of representation changes against exploitation of the current best profile/aggregation setup.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile settings with scvi_n200 encoder (config_005, 0.650 accuracy) outperform others. This experiment tests whether switching aggregation from avgpool to transformer (while keeping rna_encoder=scvi_n200 and multiprofile) improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method. This clarifies whether transformer aggregation is beneficial for this encoder/profile combination, balancing exploitation of strong scvi_n200 results with exploration of aggregation methods.

Existing evidence shows that scvi_n200 RNA encoder (config_006) outperforms pca_n2000 (config_005) and that multiprofile settings generally improve accuracy. This experiment tests scgpt RNA encoder in multiprofile setup with transformer aggregation, directly comparing it to scvi_n200 in similar conditions. It clarifies whether the RNA encoder choice (scgpt vs scvi_n200) is more impactful than aggregation method (transformer vs avgpool) when multiprofile is already effective.

Existing evidence shows that RNA-only models with scvi_n200 encoder and transformer aggregation achieve high accuracy (0.653). This experiment tests adding image data (resnet50) to this strong baseline, using transformer aggregation and concat fusion to isolate the impact of multimodal integration. It balances exploitation of proven RNA encoder strengths with exploration of multimodal potential, addressing a key design choice (image modality) without changing multiple factors simultaneously.

The existing evidence shows that config_032 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, concat) achieves the highest validation accuracy (0.6878). This experiment tests whether switching the fusion method from 'concat' to 'weighted' improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It builds on the strongest current configuration while exploring a key design choice with minimal changes, balancing exploitation of prior success and exploration of critical parameters.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 and resnet50 achieve high accuracy (config_033: 0.713). This experiment tests whether replacing resnet50 with the more advanced imagenet_vit_l image encoder (while keeping scvi_n200 RNA encoder, transformer aggregation, and concat fusion) improves performance. This isolates the effect of the image encoder, a critical design choice, and explores whether stronger visual representations can further enhance performance in a singleprofile setting.

Existing evidence shows multimodal models with scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l achieve high accuracy (config_038: 0.7207). This experiment tests the same RNA/image encoders but with weighted fusion instead of concat, isolating the effect of fusion method. It builds on prior success while exploring a key design choice with minimal changes, balancing exploitation of strong signals and exploration of critical components.
